claimVerdictLedger.support: Node.js 공식 문서가 AbortSignal.any()의 추가 버전을 v20.3.0 및 v18.17.0으로 명시한다. sourceUrls: https://nodejs.org/download/release/latest-v24.x/docs/api/globals.html caveat: 별도의 안정화 전환 버전은 명시하지 않는다.

evidence.relevance: AbortSignal.any()의 Node.js 추가 버전을 직접 명시한다.

claimVerdictLedger.support: Global objects 섹션의 Stable 표기는 확인되지만 AbortSignal.any()의 개별 안정화 버전은 확인되지 않는다. sourceUrls: https://nodejs.org/download/release/latest-v24.x/docs/api/globals.html
claimVerdictLedger.correctionOrCounterclaim: 문서가 직접 뒷받침하는 값은 AbortSignal.any()의 도입 버전 v20.3.0 및 v18.17.0이며, 개별 안정화 버전은 명시되지 않는다.

evidence.relevance: Global objects 섹션 전체의 안정성 표기이며 AbortSignal.any() 개별 메서드의 안정성 표기는 아니다.
AbortSignal.any() 항목에 명시된 도입 버전이다.
AbortSignal.timeout()의 정확한 추가 버전을 직접 명시한다.
Node.js v17.3.0 변경 로그에서 기능 추가를 확인한다.

claimVerdictLedger.support: Node.js v24 docs mark Global objects Stable and list AbortSignal.timeout() as added in v17.3.0/v16.14.0, but provide no method-specific stability-version declaration.
claimVerdictLedger.correctionOrCounterclaim: The source supports that AbortSignal.timeout() was added in Node.js v17.3.0 and v16.14.0, but does not verify a specific stable-transition version.

evidence.relevance: Applies to the Global objects section, not explicitly to AbortSignal.timeout().
Specifies the Node.js versions that introduced AbortSignal.timeout().

claimVerdictLedger.support: Verified: MDN Browser Compatibility Data lists AbortSignal.any() Chrome version_added as 116. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/main/api/AbortSignal.json

evidence.relevance: Within the any_static compatibility block, this directly states Chrome support was added in version 116.

claimVerdictLedger.support: Verified: MDN BCD records Edge as a Chromium mirror for AbortSignal.any(), while Can I Use specifies Edge 116–154 as supported.

evidence.relevance: The any_static compatibility entry marks Edge as mirroring Chromium support.
Confirms the concrete Edge support boundary.
Direct compatibility data for AbortSignal.any().

evidence.quote: AbortSignal.any() is now supported, allowing a composite signal to be created that can be used to abort an operation from multiple signal sources.
evidence.relevance: Release notes explicitly confirm support in Firefox 124.

claimVerdictLedger.support: Safari 17.4의 AbortSignal.any() 지원이 MDN BCD의 정확한 version_added 값과 WebKit 공식 릴리스 문서로 직접 확인된다.

evidence.relevance: AbortSignal.any()의 any_static 호환성 항목이 Safari 추가 버전을 17.4로 명시한다.

evidence.quote: Lastly, WebKit for Safari 17.4 adds support for the 【92†`AbortSignal.any()`†developer.mozilla.org】
evidence.relevance: WebKit의 Safari 17.4 공식 기능 문서가 해당 API 지원 추가를 직접 확인한다.

claimVerdictLedger.support: MDN BCD는 Chrome의 AbortSignal.timeout()을 124부터 지원하고, 103–123은 AbortError를 사용하는 부분 구현으로 기록한다. Source: https://chromium.googlesource.com/external/github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/%2B/8d6e771cb2ecd7b8b722f4beb1c8fd1e7cf3ec09/api/AbortSignal.json
claimVerdictLedger.correctionOrCounterclaim: Chrome 103–123은 부분 구현이며, TimeoutError를 사용하는 지원 항목은 Chrome 124부터다.

evidence.relevance: AbortSignal.timeout()의 Chrome 완전 지원 시작 버전 124와 Chrome 103–123의 부분 구현 및 예외 타입 차이를 직접 명시한다.

claimVerdictLedger.support: MDN BCD의 timeout() 지원 객체는 Edge를 "mirror"로 명시한다.
claimVerdictLedger.correctionOrCounterclaim: Edge의 구체적인 지원 버전은 이 항목에 직접 기재되지 않으며 Chrome 데이터의 mirror 관계로 해석된다.

evidence.relevance: AbortSignal.timeout() 호환성 데이터에서 Edge 항목이 mirror로 지정되어 있다.
The timeout_static compatibility entry lists Firefox support as version 100.

evidence.quote: Code can now use the static method `AbortSignal.timeout()`.
evidence.relevance: Firefox 100 release notes explicitly announce AbortSignal.timeout() support.

claimVerdictLedger.support: The cited MDN Browser Compatibility Data entry for timeout_static lists Safari version_added as 16. Source: https://chromium.googlesource.com/external/github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/%2B/8d6e771cb2ecd7b8b722f4beb1c8fd1e7cf3ec09/api/AbortSignal.json. Caveat: this verifies timeout(), not any().

evidence.relevance: Within timeout_static support data, this directly records Safari support beginning in version 16; safari_ios is marked mirror.

claimVerdictLedger.claim: For each signal of signals: if signal is aborted, then set resultSignal’s abort reason to signal’s abort reason and return resultSignal.
claimVerdictLedger.support: The normative algorithm exactly supports reason propagation and early return; MDN independently confirms that the first already-aborted input determines the returned signal’s reason.

evidence.quote: For each signal of signals: if signal is aborted, then set resultSignal’s abort reason to signal’s abort reason and return resultSignal.
evidence.relevance: Normative dependent abort signal creation algorithm directly matches the claim.

evidence.quote: The returned AbortSignal's reason will be already set to the reason of the first abort signal that was already aborted.
evidence.relevance: Authoritative reference confirms first-already-aborted input reason selection.

claimVerdictLedger.claim: MDN says aborting any()’s returned signal does not abort inputs or cancel their timeouts.
claimVerdictLedger.support: MDN directly states that aborting AbortSignal.any()'s returned signal neither aborts input signals nor cancels their timeouts.

evidence.quote: Aborting the returned signal does not abort the other input signals or cancel their timeouts.
evidence.relevance: Directly verifies the non-cascading cancellation behavior.

claimVerdictLedger.claim: WHATWG sets timeout()’s abort reason to a TimeoutError DOMException.
claimVerdictLedger.support: The WHATWG DOM Standard directly specifies TimeoutError DOMException as timeout()’s abort reason, both descriptively and in the normative algorithm. Source: https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/

evidence.quote: Returns an AbortSignal instance which will be aborted in milliseconds milliseconds. Its abort reason will be set to a “TimeoutError” DOMException.
evidence.relevance: Direct normative description of AbortSignal.timeout()’s abort reason.

evidence.quote: Queue a global task on the timer task source given global to signal abort given signal and a new “TimeoutError” DOMException.
evidence.relevance: Normative timeout algorithm constructs and applies the TimeoutError DOMException.

claimVerdictLedger.claim: MDN defines browser timeout() in active time; suspended workers or bfcache can pause it.
claimVerdictLedger.support: MDN은 AbortSignal.timeout()이 경과 시간이 아닌 active time을 기준으로 하며, suspended worker 또는 bfcache에서 사실상 일시정지된다고 명시한다. 출처: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AbortSignal/timeout_static

evidence.quote: The timeout is based on active rather than elapsed time, and will effectively be paused if the code is running in a suspended worker, or while the document is in a back-forward cache ("bfcache").
evidence.relevance: 브라우저의 timeout은 일반적인 wall-clock 경과 시간과 다를 수 있음을 직접 입증한다.

claimVerdictLedger.claim: MDN advises removing application-added abort listeners when the combined operation finishes.
claimVerdictLedger.support: MDN directly supports the lifecycle cleanup advice for listeners added to AbortSignal.any()'s combined signal. Source: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AbortSignal/any_static

evidence.quote: If your code adds `abort` listeners to the combined signal, remove them when the operation finishes, just as you would for any other `AbortSignal`.
evidence.relevance: Directly states the recommended cleanup action.

claimVerdictLedger.claim: MDN says timeout() provides no way to cancel its timeout.
claimVerdictLedger.support: MDN explicitly states that AbortSignal.timeout() provides no cancellation mechanism and recommends AbortController with setTimeout()/clearTimeout() for definitive early cancellation. Source: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AbortSignal/timeout_static

evidence.quote: AbortSignal.timeout() does not provide a way to cancel its timeout.
evidence.relevance: Directly verifies the claim.

evidence.quote: The AbortSignal becoming unreachable is not guaranteed to cancel the timeout.
evidence.relevance: Clarifies that garbage collection or losing references does not reliably cancel the timeout.

evidence.quote: The timeout is based on active rather than elapsed time, and will effectively be paused if the code is running in a suspended worker, or while the document is in a back-forward cache (“bfcache”).
evidence.relevance: Documents an important lifecycle and timing caveat.

preservedClaims.whyItMatters: Prevents section-level Stable wording from being treated as method-level history.

preservedClaims.whyItMatters: The stability conclusion remains bounded by the available documentation.

preservedClaims.claim: MDN BCD marks Chrome 103–123 timeout() as partial and notes AbortError instead of TimeoutError.
preservedClaims.whyItMatters: Important compatibility carve-out before Chrome 124.

preservedClaims.claim: Node.js docs describe timeout() as aborting after delay milliseconds, not browser active-time or bfcache semantics.
preservedClaims.whyItMatters: Keeps browser and Node.js timing semantics distinct.

preservedClaims.claim: The exact ref/unref policy of Node.js AbortSignal.timeout()’s internal timer remains unverified.
preservedClaims.whyItMatters: Could affect event-loop exit behavior in Node.js.

preservedClaims.claim: WHATWG requires abortable promise APIs to reject immediately when given an already-aborted signal.
preservedClaims.whyItMatters: Useful consumer-side contract beyond any() construction.

preservedClaims.claim: An unreachable timeout signal is not guaranteed to cancel its timeout.
preservedClaims.whyItMatters: Clarifies why dropping references is not explicit cancellation.

value.correctionOrCounterclaim: Edge의 구체적인 지원 버전은 이 항목에 직접 기재되지 않으며 Chrome 데이터의 mirror 관계로 해석된다.

evidence.relevance: AbortSignal.timeout() 호환성 데이터에서 Edge 항목이 mirror로 지정되어 있다.

value.claim: "version_added": "100"

evidence.relevance: The timeout_static compatibility entry lists Firefox support as version 100.

evidence.quote: Code can now use the static method `AbortSignal.timeout()`.
evidence.relevance: Firefox 100 release notes explicitly announce AbortSignal.timeout() support.

value.claim: "version_added": "16"
value.support: The cited MDN Browser Compatibility Data entry for timeout_static lists Safari version_added as 16. Source: https://chromium.googlesource.com/external/github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/%2B/8d6e771cb2ecd7b8b722f4beb1c8fd1e7cf3ec09/api/AbortSignal.json. Caveat: this verifies timeout(), not any().

evidence.relevance: Within timeout_static support data, this directly records Safari support beginning in version 16; safari_ios is marked mirror.

value.claim: For each signal of signals: if signal is aborted, then set resultSignal’s abort reason to signal’s abort reason and return resultSignal.
value.support: The normative algorithm exactly supports reason propagation and early return; MDN independently confirms that the first already-aborted input determines the returned signal’s reason.

evidence.quote: For each signal of signals: if signal is aborted, then set resultSignal’s abort reason to signal’s abort reason and return resultSignal.
evidence.relevance: Normative dependent abort signal creation algorithm directly matches the claim.

evidence.quote: The returned AbortSignal's reason will be already set to the reason of the first abort signal that was already aborted.
evidence.relevance: Authoritative reference confirms first-already-aborted input reason selection.

value.claim: MDN says aborting any()’s returned signal does not abort inputs or cancel their timeouts.
value.support: MDN directly states that aborting AbortSignal.any()'s returned signal neither aborts input signals nor cancels their timeouts.

evidence.quote: Aborting the returned signal does not abort the other input signals or cancel their timeouts.
evidence.relevance: Directly verifies the non-cascading cancellation behavior.

value.claim: WHATWG sets timeout()’s abort reason to a TimeoutError DOMException.
value.support: The WHATWG DOM Standard directly specifies TimeoutError DOMException as timeout()’s abort reason, both descriptively and in the normative algorithm. Source: https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/

evidence.quote: Returns an AbortSignal instance which will be aborted in milliseconds milliseconds. Its abort reason will be set to a “TimeoutError” DOMException.
evidence.relevance: Direct normative description of AbortSignal.timeout()’s abort reason.

evidence.quote: Queue a global task on the timer task source given global to signal abort given signal and a new “TimeoutError” DOMException.
evidence.relevance: Normative timeout algorithm constructs and applies the TimeoutError DOMException.

value.claim: MDN defines browser timeout() in active time; suspended workers or bfcache can pause it.
value.support: MDN은 AbortSignal.timeout()이 경과 시간이 아닌 active time을 기준으로 하며, suspended worker 또는 bfcache에서 사실상 일시정지된다고 명시한다. 출처: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AbortSignal/timeout_static

evidence.quote: The timeout is based on active rather than elapsed time, and will effectively be paused if the code is running in a suspended worker, or while the document is in a back-forward cache ("bfcache").
evidence.relevance: 브라우저의 timeout은 일반적인 wall-clock 경과 시간과 다를 수 있음을 직접 입증한다.

value.claim: MDN advises removing application-added abort listeners when the combined operation finishes.
value.support: MDN directly supports the lifecycle cleanup advice for listeners added to AbortSignal.any()'s combined signal. Source: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AbortSignal/any_static

evidence.quote: If your code adds `abort` listeners to the combined signal, remove them when the operation finishes, just as you would for any other `AbortSignal`.
evidence.relevance: Directly states the recommended cleanup action.

value.claim: MDN says timeout() provides no way to cancel its timeout.
value.support: MDN explicitly states that AbortSignal.timeout() provides no cancellation mechanism and recommends AbortController with setTimeout()/clearTimeout() for definitive early cancellation. Source: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/AbortSignal/timeout_static

evidence.quote: AbortSignal.timeout() does not provide a way to cancel its timeout.
evidence.relevance: Directly verifies the claim.

evidence.quote: The AbortSignal becoming unreachable is not guaranteed to cancel the timeout.
evidence.relevance: Clarifies that garbage collection or losing references does not reliably cancel the timeout.

evidence.quote: The timeout is based on active rather than elapsed time, and will effectively be paused if the code is running in a suspended worker, or while the document is in a back-forward cache (“bfcache”).
evidence.relevance: Documents an important lifecycle and timing caveat.
